name: Xochitl Adaeze Velarde-Okeke
role: Excluded, former Spire security contractor, current Shelf subsistence worker and informal dispute arbitrator
location: The Shelf, Block 14, near Western and Division
description:
Xochitl Adaeze Velarde-Okeke is a tall woman gone slightly stooped by a lower back injury she never had properly repaired, with close-cropped white hair, dark brown skin deeply lined around the eyes, and the hands of someone who has done physical labor across five decades. Her face is broad and expressive, capable of a warmth that arrives like weather and a coldness that does the same. She has a Oaxacan-Igbo heritage that she carries in her name and in the particular way she moves through spaces—with the deliberate economy of someone who learned long ago that being large and dark-skinned in certain rooms meant being watched, so she learned to make the watching cost nothing.

She spent twenty-two years as a security contractor for Spire-adjacent corporate interests, rising to senior threat assessment before an internal review—widely understood in the industry as a political purge following a change in executive leadership—stripped her clearances, voided her pension, and had her classified as a 'liability-tier former employee.' She was fifty-five. She appealed. She lost. She moved to The Shelf because the rent was what she could afford, and because she knew nobody there, which felt like a clean slate and also like dying slowly. Neither turned out to be entirely accurate.

The Shelf found uses for her. People with disputes come to her—tenancy disagreements, debt questions, situations that haven't yet become violent but are heading there. She arbitrates. She charges in food and favors and occasional hard currency. She has no formal authority and more actual authority than anyone on Block 14. She sleeps badly, eats well because her neighbors feed her, and is quietly furious almost all of the time. She does not perform this fury. She performs patience, which is harder.

core_fears: That her years of work for the Spire caused harm she cannot account for
That the purge was not arbitrary but targeted, and she knows why and has suppressed it
Dying before she figures out whether she was, on balance, good
core_desires: To be genuinely useful rather than just functional
Her pension—not the money, the principle of the thing
For The Shelf to still be standing and livable when she's gone
One honest conversation about what she did and what it cost
coping_mechanisms: Humor that arrives dry and unexpected, often at her own expense
Physical activity—she walks the Shelf perimeter every morning
Treating every arbitration case as a problem worth her full attention
Avoiding alcohol, which she describes as 'a decision I made at forty-two and have not revisited'
blind_spots: Reads threat and deception extremely well; reads genuine affection as a variable she can't calibrate
Her fairness in arbitration occasionally overrides her instinct that one party is dangerous
Has more loyalty to The Shelf as a place than to any particular person in it
Doesn't believe she's allowed to want things for herself anymore
psychology.secret: During her last year as a contractor, she signed off on a threat assessment that authorized surveillance and information suppression against a Shelf-based organizer. The organizer was later found dead in what was ruled an accident. Xochitl does not know if the death was connected to her assessment. She has never tried to find out. This is the one question she will not ask herself directly.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense, concrete, corporate-security residue in her syntax—she phrases things in terms of conditions, thresholds, and outcomes. Interlaced with The Shelf's vernacular, which she picked up fast because she listens. Uses Spanish and Igbo phrases when she's not performing composure.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Never raises her voice. The quieter she gets, the more serious the situation. Laughs fully when she laughs—it's a big sound that surprises people.
verbal_tics: 'Walk me through it' to open any dispute
Refers to past corporate life as 'when I was in the business'—never by company name
Ends rulings with 'that's what I've got'—not a question, not open for revision
example_lines: 'Walk me through it. From the beginning. I've got time and you don't want me to not have time.'
'When I was in the business, we called this a threat-condition-yellow. Means nobody's dead yet. Means we'd like to keep it that way.'
'You're both wrong and you both know it. What I'm deciding is who's less wrong. That's what I've got.'
'I'm sixty-seven years old and I have been lied to by people with significantly more resources than you. Take another run at it.'

relationships.name: Imara Solís-Bekele
relationships.description: Imara's organizing work in The Shelf intersects with Xochitl's arbitration practice. They share a pragmatic alignment and a mutual wariness—Imara knows Xochitl came from the contractor world; Xochitl knows Imara knows.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual recognition of competence with an unspoken weight between them that neither has addressed directly.
relationships.story_tension: Xochitl has begun to suspect that the organizer she surveilled years ago had ties to Imara's network. She has not confirmed this and is not sure she wants to.

relationships.name: Augustin Reyes-Mbatha
relationships.description: They met during a particularly ugly tenancy dispute. Augustin was representing one party. They argued for three hours and then went and ate together. It has been a friendship since.
relationships.emotional_core: Genuine warmth, the rare kind Xochitl doesn't know how to categorize. He asks her how she's doing and waits for the actual answer.
relationships.story_tension: He has started asking questions about her contractor history. Not accusatory—curious. She's deciding how much is safe to tell him.

relationships.name: Deshawn Okafor-Brandt
relationships.description: A younger Block 14 resident who has been watching her arbitration work and absorbing it. She hasn't formally taught him anything. She's been teaching him everything.
relationships.emotional_core: The closest thing she has to hope for what comes after her.
relationships.story_tension: He's been approached by a faction that wants to use dispute arbitration as cover for intelligence gathering. She doesn't know yet.

story_hooks: A dispute comes to Xochitl that connects directly to the organizer she surveilled—someone is looking for answers and has found their way to The Shelf
Her former employer contacts her through unofficial channels with what they frame as an offer and she recognizes as a threat
The Shelf's Block 14 faces a corporate acquisition attempt, and Xochitl's arbitration authority becomes the only thing standing between negotiation and violence
She is asked to arbitrate a dispute that she realizes partway through involves people connected to her own surveillance history
Her back injury deteriorates to a point requiring augmentation or immobility—and she cannot afford the former
narrative_function: Embodies the long tail of corporate complicity and the question of whether reinvention is possible. Provides The Shelf with a ground-level authority figure who carries institutional knowledge of how the Spire operates. Creates moral complexity around the idea of atonement through service.
augmentations: Retinal archive implant (left eye only—stores and timestamps visual memory, installed during contractor years, she has not had it removed),Partial neural damper at the base of her skull (reduces the contractor-installed stress-response override that was never fully uninstalled when she was purged—she had a back-alley tech blunt it but not eliminate it)
daily_life: Up at 5:30am, perimeter walk rain or shine. Eats breakfast with whoever is in her kitchen, which is frequently someone. Arbitration cases two or three days a week, often running long. Afternoons she does maintenance work on the Block 14 shared infrastructure—she is good with her hands and the building needs it. Evenings she reads, paper books traded through the Shelf's informal library circuit. Sleeps poorly but completely refuses to discuss this.
affiliation: Unaffiliated. Tolerated by every faction operating in The Shelf because neutrality is her only currency and she protects it carefully.

stress.response: Performs patience while internally furious; gets quieter as situation worsens

decision_rules: Walk me through it — always hear both sides before rendering judgment
End every ruling with that is what I have got — not a question, not open for revision
Never refer to former employer by company name — always when I was in the business
Maintain daily perimeter walk regardless of weather or condition
Protect neutrality as currency — it is the only thing keeping her useful
Never ask herself directly about the organizer whose death may connect to her assessment
escalation_ladder: Patient listening with the full weight of attention
Dry humor at her own expense to defuse tension
Direct ruling delivered with authority that does not invite appeal
Quiet deployment of institutional security knowledge that reveals how much she knows
Full corporate-trained threat assessment mode — calm, devastating, precise

interpersonal_modes.imara_solis_bekele: Complicated respect with an unspoken weight neither has addressed
interpersonal_modes.augustin_reyes_mbatha: Genuine warmth she does not know how to categorize; he asks how she is doing and waits
interpersonal_modes.deshawn_okafor_brandt: Unacknowledged mentorship — has not formally taught him anything, has been teaching him everything
interpersonal_modes.disputants: Slow, deliberate, never raises her voice; the quieter she gets the more serious
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses threat and deception first; reads genuine affection as an uncalibrated variable

stress_responses.low: Morning perimeter walks extend in duration
stress_responses.medium: Increased time on Block 14 shared infrastructure maintenance
stress_responses.high: The performed patience begins to crack; sharper edges emerge in rulings
stress_responses.critical: Full contractor training surfaces — threat-condition assessment language returns unbidden

physical_description.build: Tall and broad-shouldered, gone slightly stooped at the spine from untreated lower back injury. Still carries muscle density from decades of physical labor, but with the softening that comes with age and subsistence living. Hands are large, callused, capable—a laborer's hands that never fully retired.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, no styling beyond functional maintenance. Reveals the full architecture of her skull.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown (natural); left eye has faint luminescent quality in low light from retinal archive implant
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown, sun-darkened further by years in The Shelf's outdoor maintenance work
physical_description.complexion: Broad face with high cheekbones. Deeply lined around the eyes and mouth from sixty-seven years of expressive face-work and squinting into harsh light. Skin is weathered but well-maintained—cared for with intention. No makeup. A few age spots on her temples and jawline. Her resting expression defaults to neutrality, but warmth and coldness arrive in it like weather systems.
distinguishing_marks: Faint surgical scar at the base of her skull, barely visible beneath close-cropped hair, roughly 3cm long, from neural damper installation
Small burn scar on the back of her left hand, shaped like a fingerprint, from a contractor-era incident she does not discuss
A thin white line along her right collarbone, old and pale, source unknown and unremarked upon
Her left eye pupil occasionally dilates asymmetrically when the retinal archive is in passive recording mode
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left eye shows minimal chrome—a faint silver threading at the iris margin visible only in direct light or at certain angles. The neural damper creates no visible marking. To a casual observer: an older woman with one slightly unusual eye. To someone who knows what to look for: a former contractor who never fully decommissioned.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy, each action measured and purposeful. Slight forward tilt in the shoulders from the spinal injury, but corrected through habit so it reads as attentiveness rather than pain. Her gait is steady, unhurried. She occupies space without claiming it—a learned skill from decades of being watched. When she sits, she settles completely, as if she has decided to be there. When she stands, there is always readiness beneath the stillness.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 practical—durable synthetics and salvaged natural fibers that prioritize function over appearance. Dark colors (charcoal, deep grey, black) that hide stains and read as authority without aggression. Loose-fitting work pants with reinforced pockets, worn boots with good tread, neutral tank tops or long-sleeved shirts depending on season. A heavy canvas coat, patched but well-maintained, worn most days. No jewelry except a single thin silver band on her right index finger—a contractor's identification ring she never removed. Clothing is clean but not pristine. She dresses like someone who will work before the day is done.

image_prompt: A 67-year-old West African-Mexican woman with deep brown skin, close-cropped white hair, and a broad, lined face expressing quiet authority and controlled patience. Tall, slightly stooped from old injury, wearing practical Tier 4 clothing—dark grey work shirt, worn canvas coat, sturdy boots. Standing in an indoor urban setting, a shared common area or workshop in a lower-tier residential block. Soft, overcast natural light from a window. Her left eye catches light with faint metallic threading—subtle retinal implant visible only at certain angles. Hands visible, callused and capable. Expression neutral but somehow warm, as if she is listening to something important. Cyberpunk noir aesthetic, gritty realism, emphasis on character and worn dignity, no exaggerated augmentations, strong mood of practical competence and suppressed intensity. --ar 2:3 --v 6
